thread.title_full: Sen. Jon Husted outlines support for photo ID voting requirements in op-ed

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Sen. Jon Husted outlines support for photo ID voting requirements in op-ed
text:
Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) outlined his support for national photo identification requirements for voters in an op-ed published by the Washington Reporter, according to an April 22 statement. Husted said his experience as Ohio Secretary of State informed his position and pointed to Ohio’s recent election turnout as evidence that such measures can work.
The topic of voter identification has become a central issue in discussions about election integrity across the United States. Husted said that requiring a photo ID would make it “easy to vote and hard to cheat,” reflecting ongoing debates about how best to secure elections while ensuring access.
In the op-ed, Husted wrote, “Before joining the U.S. Senate, Ohioans trusted me to serve as their chief elections officer, electing me two times as Ohio Secretary of State.” He continued, “My mission was simple: to make it easy to vote and hard to cheat.” As Secretary of State, he said he focused on maintaining accurate voter rolls and preventing individuals from being registered in multiple places.
Husted also noted that Ohio now requires photo ID at polling places and cited high voter turnout during the 2024 presidential election. “Americans show their ID every day — when entering government buildings, at the grocery store, to stay at a hotel, to start a job, or to rent a car,” he wrote. He added that more than 80 percent of Americans support requiring photo ID for voting.
He explained that while Democrats voiced some support for aspects of voter identification laws during discussions with him, every Senate Democrat voted against his proposed amendment requiring various forms of government-issued IDs at polls by a margin of 53-47 votes. “But this is not over,” Husted wrote. “Americans deserve confidence in their elections, supported by integrity measures like photo ID.”
Husted’s background includes serving as Speaker of the Ohio House of Representatives where he advanced tax reductions and educational choice scholarships according to the official website . He later served as secretary of state and lieutenant governor before joining the U.S. Senate according to the official website . In addition, he serves on several Senate committees related to health, education, labor and pensions; small business; environment; public works; and aging according to the official website .
Husted earned both bachelor’s and master’s degrees from the University of Dayton according to the official website , and raised three children with his wife Tina while living in Columbus according to the official website .
Concluding his op-ed on future efforts regarding election security legislation nationwide, Husted stated: “I look forward to continuing to work with my colleagues in the Senate to bring what Ohio has achieved to the rest of the country: making it easy to vote and hard to cheat.”
